manifest.title: Zero velocity at the top is not zero acceleration
manifest.summary: A tossed ball rises, stops for an instant at its top and falls, while a held ball is released from rest at that same instant. Both carry velocity and acceleration arrows, and the acceleration stays -9.8 m/s^2 throughout free flight.
assumptions: Constant downward acceleration of 9.8 m/s^2, no air resistance, up is positive.
The held ball is supported by the gate (zero acceleration) until the apex instant, then falls freely.
manifest.description: On the left a tossed ball rises from a launch mark to a dashed top line and falls back. On the right a held ball rests on a release gate at launch height; the gate opens at the instant the tossed ball reaches its top. Each ball has a velocity arrow v that shrinks to a dot at the top and then points down, and a downward acceleration arrow a of constant length in free flight. A height scale in metres runs beside the scene.

composition.title: Zero velocity at the top is not zero acceleration
composition.cardDescription: Toss a ball up at 3.0 to 5.0 m/s. At its top the velocity is zero, yet the acceleration stays -9.8 m/s^2 at every launch speed. No air resistance.

plan.title: Zero velocity at the top is not zero acceleration
plan.story: Maya tossed the ball up, waited for it to hang at the top, and swung. It had already dropped below her racket. If it stopped, how was it still accelerating? Her friend held a ball at shoulder height and let go. It began at zero velocity, and gravity immediately gave it downward speed. Her own ball had passed through the same moment. She tossed it faster, from 3.0 up to 5.0 m/s: the top came later and higher, but at the top the velocity was always zero and the acceleration was still 9.8 m/s^2 downward. Zero was one of the values the velocity passed through; the acceleration never changed.
plan.cardDescription: Toss a ball up at 3.0 to 5.0 m/s. At its top the velocity is zero, yet the acceleration stays -9.8 m/s^2 at every launch speed. No air resistance.
plan.learningGoal: Explain why acceleration is not zero when velocity is zero at the top of a throw, at any launch speed.

scene.description: A tossed ball rises from a launch mark and falls; a second ball is held by a release gate until the apex instant. Up is positive and both share one height scale. A velocity arrow and an acceleration arrow sit on each ball and update with the scrubber; the launch speed moves the apex.

A faster throw reaches its top later and higher; at the top the velocity reads zero and the acceleration still reads -9.8 m/s^2.

controls.label: Play
controls.purpose: Run the motion and replay it.
controls.selectionReason: Time explains the change, and the one supported transport drives every linked view.

controls.label: Time from the top
controls.purpose: Inspect any instant of the motion.
controls.selectionReason: A scrubber lets the learner stop on the instants the explanation compares.

controls.label: Launch speed
controls.purpose: Test whether the acceleration at the top depends on how fast the ball was thrown.
controls.selectionReason: The speed varies continuously and intermediate speeds show that the top moves while the acceleration does not; two named cases would hide that.

controls.label: Show arrows
controls.purpose: Hide the velocity and acceleration arrows to read the motion from the balls and the readouts alone.
controls.selectionReason: Two named states, on and off, are clearer as choice buttons than a slider; the program renderer has no native Boolean switch, so the planned two-option select is used (section 4).

assumptions: Constant downward acceleration of 9.8 m/s^2, no air resistance, up is positive.
limitations: An idealized vertical throw; real balls feel drag.

claims.text: Acceleration is -9.8 m/s^2 at every instant of free flight, including the top.
claims.check: Differentiate v = u - g t: the slope is -g at every t.

claims.text: The acceleration readout stays -9.8 m/s^2 at every launch speed from 3.0 to 5.0 m/s, including at the top.
claims.check: v = u - g t has slope -g for every u, so a = -g whatever the launch speed.

findings.message: The tossed ball's downward acceleration arrow runs through the launch-mark line and the 'Launch mark' label, between 'ma' and 'rk'.
The 'a' label of the tossed ball's acceleration arrow sits on the launch-mark line, right above the 'Launch mark' text.
The held ball's acceleration arrow runs through the 'Release gate' label, between 'ga' and 'te', and next to the open gate leg.
The held ball's 'v' label overlaps the 'Release gate' text and the gate leg, and the held ball's acceleration arrow crosses the 'Release gate' label.
The tossed ball's 'a' label sits on the launch-mark line and the 'Launch mark' text.
The tossed ball's downward velocity arrow runs through the 'Launch mark' label.
The falling held ball covers the 'Release gate' label, so it reads 'Relea... gate'.

This sample is at the landing instant, not at the top. At 5 m/s it shows the later, higher top line (1.276 m) but not that velocity reads zero at the top, so the 'apexMoves' observation cannot be judged at the maximum launch speed.
The tossed ball's long downward velocity arrow runs through the 'Launch mark' label.

At launch (u = 3 m/s) the tossed ball's velocity arrow is 30 px tall, so its 'v' label sits right on the dashed top line (around y≈190). The line runs through the label. Move the label beside the arrow tip or shorten the line so they no longer collide.
